Definition: from σιωπή (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water):--dumb, (hold) peace.
BiblicalUsage: Siopao means to hold one's peace, to be dumb, to be still, and it marks the silence of the guilty and the silence of the innocent alike. The Pharisees held their peace when Jesus asked whether it was lawful to do good on the Sabbath, the crowd charged blind Bartimaeus to hold his peace, and Jesus Himself held His peace before the high priest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus' silence before the high priest is the loudest word in the trial. I hold that there is a time to speak and a time to let the silence accuse.
